NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants. It has a collaboration with Cisco to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms. Nvidia's (NVDA) stock rocketed more than 30% Monday after the company's board announced it reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and president of the chip giant. The chip giant added nearly $1 trillion to its market cap, posting its best day since May 2023. Shares of neoclouds CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) also climbed more than 30%. In a statement Monday, Nvidia's board said it had a series of discussions with Huang and was satisfied with his candor and ability to lead the company. "The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said. Follow live updates and reactions to Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO > "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's CFO," he added. Just last week, Jones told investors during the company's Q3 earnings call that Nvidia had no plans to bring back Huang. Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12 after an alleged affair with Alice Huang, suspected of being a Chinese spy. Huang admitted to having an affair at the time but didn't name the woman. He also allegedly had affairs with two Nvidia employees, including executive Kimberly Powell. Alice Huang was the executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is suspected of smuggling high-powered Nvidia chips to China. The company said the board received input from senior levels of the US government and, based on that input, doesn't believe Huang's reinstatement poses a national security risk. "I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry, and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work," he added. title: Nvidia Vaults Higher As Jensen Huang Returns As CEO; Is Nvidia Stock A Sell Now? - Investor's Business Daily
content:
BREAKING: Nvidia Board 'Unanimously' Votes To Bring Back Jensen Huang Nvidia (NVDA) shares soared more than 30% during Monday's session after the artificial intelligence chipmaker said it has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia stock was slammed last week and lost 23%, deepening losses for investors after a six-week drop amid news of Huang's exit from the company on Nov. 12. Is Nvidia A Buy Or Sell Now? Huang resigned not long after The New York Times reported on Oct. 29 that the Nvidia executive had an affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy and business executive at Singapore-based tech company Megaspeed. But Nvidia on Monday said it board "voted unanimously" to bring back Huang effectively immediately, and that it's "confident" that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk." Nvidia had named Colette Kress, its chief financial officer, as interim CEO. Last week, the Commerce Department tightened restrictions on China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips in overseas data centers. Also, Nvidia established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to ensure compliance with U.S. export rules. Nvidia and Huang were facing investigations on several fronts in the wake of the affair revelation. Last week, California's Justice Department served a subpoena to inquire whether Nvidia's advanced chips or confidential information "may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public." Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify in front of the several House of Representatives committees on Dec. 1. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is also expected to testify. Kress has also been requested to appear on Capitol Hill to discuss Nvidia's chip exports. Huang has also agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. On Nov. 17, the AI chipmaker posted third-quarter adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share on sales of $116 billion. Sales grew 103% while adjusted earnings jumped 111%. Analysts polled by FactSet were targeting earnings of $2.49 per share and sales of $109.3 billion. Data center revenue vaulted 110% from the prior year. Meanwhile, Nvidia's fourth-quarter sales guidance came in at $130 billion vs. views of $125 billion. Needham maintained its price target of $200 noting "strong demand coupled with increased supply" in fiscal 2028. Nvidia's Relative Strength Rating has fallen to 19. The AI chip behemoth still has a top-level Earnings Per Share Rating of 99, though. The stock's all-around strength, or Composite Rating, lags at 49. Funds own 41% of the company's outstanding shares, according to IBD MarketSurge research. But the stock's Accumulation/Distribution Rating of E confirms that funds have joined retail sellers of the stock amid the scandal. title: 'Jensen's judgment remains under question': What Wall Street analysts are saying about Huang's comeback - Business Insider
content: Investors are in rally mode on Monday after Jensen Huang's comeback, but the Nvidia chief's return hasn't removed all of the uncertainty hanging over the stock, Wall Street analysts say. Several forecasters raised questions about Nvidia's future even with Jensen Huang back at the helm of the chipmaker. That's largely because the investigation into Huang's affairs and whether the CEO's actions were a national security risk is still ongoing. Meanwhile, questions still linger around Nvidia's China business and its AI deals, which face a possible slowdown as the chipmaker has drawn more scrutiny, market pros say. Nvidia shares embarked on a historic rally on Monday, marking this largest market-cap gain for a stock ever, but the stock is still down more than 30% from its early October high. Analysts at Bernstein said they see "some overhangs" for Nvidia that could limit the stock's upside potential. In light of Huang's affairs, the CEO's trustworthiness still is still under question, and the weaknesses in Nvidia's board and corporate governance has also been "clearly highlighted," the firm wrote in a note to clients on Monday. "Jensen's judgment remains under question. We don't actually care what Jensen does on his personal time. However, he clearly does keep questionable company on occasion, and his willingness to lie to the board and other key stakeholders is troubling to us," the note said, adding that the investigation into Huang is still ongoing. "While we are happy to have Jensen back, the on-again-off-again response from the board, is, frankly, clown-like (they were adamant just last week that he was gone for sure) and brings up legitimate questions as to their judgment and process which has to make one wonder how they come to their other important decisions," the analysts added. The firm noted that investors remain worried about the "achievability" of AI spending. Bernstein upgraded its rating on Nvidia to "outperform," but reiterated its $ 200-a-share price target, which was slashed from the prior $400 last week as reports of Huang's second alleged affair came to light. Dan Ives, a prominent tech bull, also said he had some reservations about the stock, even with Huang back at the helm. In a note to clients, the Yorkville Ives senior managing director said he was reiterating his $225 price target on the stock, down from the prior $300 per share. "We are maintaining our Outperform rating and $225 price target rather than moving to the with-Jensen case today, and the reason is the sequence of what still has to close. The independent committee's investigation is ongoing, the government inquiries the company says it is cooperating with are ongoing, the export question has not been resolved," Ives wrote, referring to Nvidia's business in China. "Our framework is unchanged, and the gap between $225 and $300 is the value of Jensen with the governance questions behind him, not Jensen alone," he added. Luke Lango, an independent tech analyst, said described the stock surge following Huang's return as a "relief rally and nothing more," as the Nvidia CEO being reinstated does nothing to alleviate fears of an AI capex slowdown. "The bull case — that the 'Bank of Nvidia' is open again and the AI buildout proceeds as planned — is flawed," he wrote, adding that it was more likely Huang would pull back on dealmaking after coming back to the chipmaker. "Fresh off a very public scandal, he's unlikely to restart that machine," he said. Some analysts said they're looking at Nvidia with more optimism now. RBC analysts said Huang being reinstated at Nvidia has strengthened the bull case for the stock, as it alleviates fears that the company could see an exodus of talent with Huang gone. "NVDA's business fundamentals remain strong," the firm said, though analysts noted they expected the investigations into export restrictions "and other issues" to continue.

content: News that Jensen Huang will be returning as CEO of Nvidia was like jet fuel for the market on Monday, but short-seller Carson Block is still skeptical. title: NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director - NVIDIA Newsroom
content: NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair. “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.” As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it. The Board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The committee is engaging counsel with experience in national security matters, and such counsel will be retaining advisors with expertise in national security matters. NVIDIA is commencing a search to fill a new position, Chief Compliance Officer, to oversee compliance across NVIDIA and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.
